binders: n is universally quantified over the natural numbers, including 0.
schemeError and perturbationError are arbitrary functions Fin n -> Real, equivalently arbitrary real vectors with n coordinates.
conclusions: sqrt(sum over i : Fin n of (schemeError(i) + perturbationError(i))^2) <= sqrt(sum over i : Fin n of schemeError(i)^2) + sqrt(sum over i : Fin n of perturbationError(i)^2).
mathematical_definitions: For x,y : Fin n -> Real, their coordinatewise sum is defined by (x + y)(i) = x(i) + y(i).
For x : Fin n -> Real, define ||x||_2 = sqrt(sum over i : Fin n of x(i)^2).
The constant exponent 2 denotes ordinary real squaring, and all sums range over every one of the n coordinates.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every natural-number dimension n and every two real n-vectors schemeError and perturbationError, the Euclidean norm of their coordinatewise sum is at most the sum of their Euclidean norms.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The proposition is restricted to finite-dimensional vectors indexed by Fin n and to real-valued coordinates.
There are no hypotheses on either vector; in particular, their coordinates need not be nonnegative and the names do not impose any interpretation as actual errors.

The dimension is not required to be positive. When n = 0, both function domains are empty, every sum is the empty sum 0, and the conclusion reduces to 0 <= 0; this is a degenerate case rather than an empty universal quantification.
Although Real.sqrt is defined for negative inputs by first truncating them to zero, every square-root argument in this proposition is a sum of squares and is therefore nonnegative.
The proposition encodes only the norm inequality. It does not characterize equality, assert strictness, identify maximizing vectors, or relate the two vectors to any external computational process.
